content.value: This is the ONE design fork the Connectors charter has never made. P0 landed the tenant seam (chat_sessions.owner_workspace_id, RequireChatAccess, tenant-scoped /v1/chat). Now we choose HOW a Cloud tenant's agent actually runs — sandboxed, per-workspace, no host access — and we choose it with a MEASURED cold-start number, not a vibe. The Linear 10s wall is the acceptance criterion.

This Paper is the wave's living story. Strategize (now) sets direction + the survey plan. Digest appends the survey digest + the verify/benchmark fleet BEFORE it flies. Decide ratifies D10 with quoted numbers + the wave plan BEFORE builders fly. Review closes it as the debrief. Fable is out of credits this run: every Fable phase is pinned to Opus; every builder is builder_model:opus; no verify/build agent is ever routed to Fable.

blocks.text: The wish (verbatim intent)

content.value: Resolve D10 with REAL cold-start numbers, then stand up the per-workspace sandboxed runner far enough to prove ONE isolated agent turn. Candidates (charter): (a) Vercel Sandbox — Firecracker microVM, GA, native to our Vercel stack, preserves the claude-CLI-subprocess shape; (b) containers with our own orchestration; (c) an API-based agent that never shells out (naturally multi-tenant but a DIFFERENT engine than today's Studio chat). HARD BAR: first agent response <=10s cold-start, because Linear's AgentSession marks agents unresponsive past 10s — a MEASURED acceptance criterion. The runner runs per-workspace with NO host access and connector-scoped credentials (reverses bypassPermissions for Cloud; that survives only self-hosted). Memory = the workspace-owned Barkpark Session (owner_workspace_id landed in P0). Deliver: (1) a ratified D10 decision backed by ACTUAL benchmark output — where a candidate needs infra/credentials we lack headless, design the harness + name the exact human-gated measurement step rather than guessing; (2) a decision paper/charter update; (3) if the winner can be stood up far enough to prove one isolated turn this wave, do it, else file the build as the next slice with the harness in place. Extend task-6672a70bea19dc11, do NOT duplicate it. Do NOT start P2 or any channel work.

blocks.text: The strategic direction for this wave

content.value: Today's engine (self-hosted / operator profile, D5) is api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/claude_chat.ex: it spawns the claude CLI via Port.open({:spawn_executable, @shell}, ...) at line ~853, injecting env at the env: seam (~line 409), with FULL host access and bypassPermissions allowed. That shape is exactly what Cloud CANNOT have. D10 asks: what replaces Port.open for a tenant, and can the replacement answer within 10 seconds cold?
My lean, to be pressure-tested by two explore rounds — NOT yet ratified:

items.value: LEAN TOWARD (a) Vercel Sandbox as primary. Firecracker microVM, GA, native to our Vercel stack, and it PRESERVES the claude-CLI-subprocess shape — the enormous claude_chat.ex machinery (arg building, env injection, permission modes, SSE streaming via Recorder, session resume) can be reused with Port.open swapped for a sandbox exec, not rewritten. Candidate (c) the API-based agent is naturally multi-tenant but a DIFFERENT engine: it forks Studio chat into two brains. Reuse beats a second engine unless (a) blows the 10s wall.

THE CRUX IS COLD-START COMPOSITION, not microVM boot. First-response latency = microVM boot + getting the claude binary present (preinstalled snapshot vs per-boot install — the likely killer) + claude auth status (probe.ex already MEASURES ~1-2s on guerrilla) + model first-token. A per-boot npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code almost certainly blows 10s; a prebuilt snapshot or a WARM POOL of pre-booted sandboxes is the mitigation. The benchmark must DECOMPOSE these, not report one opaque number.

WARM-POOL is probably mandatory and we have prior art: the deploy-with-barkpark builder off-box warm-pool concept (NOT live) is the same shape. Whichever runner wins, N pre-booted sandboxes per region is how you beat 10s cold — so cold-start has TWO honest numbers: true-cold (first ever) and warm-pool-hit (steady state). Decide which the 10s bar governs.

CONNECTOR-SCOPED CREDENTIALS + NO HOST ACCESS is a design deliverable of THIS wave even if the build is deferred: the env: injection seam is where host creds get replaced by connector-scoped creds, and bypassPermissions must be forced OFF for the Cloud profile. Map exactly which claude_chat.ex knobs flip.

HONESTY OVER A FABRICATED NUMBER: Vercel Sandbox real cold-start needs a Vercel account/token we may not have headless (VERCEL_PLATFORM_TOKEN is a human gate). If we cannot measure it here, the deliverable is a RUNNABLE harness + the exact human-gated command, plus every number we CAN measure locally (claude cold-start, container boot, API first-token). A benchmark claim with no quoted output is vacuous green.

SCOPE DISCIPLINE: research+decision wave. Prove one isolated turn is the stretch build; if the winner needs the human-gated account, file the build slice with the harness in place rather than faking a turn. Do NOT touch P2 (Chat SDK bridge) or channel adapters.

blocks.text: DIGEST · 2026-07-13 · 13 survey reports folded · 6-agent verify/benchmark fleet in flight
Digest — what the survey established

content.value: Reuse-beats-rewrite is confirmed at the code level. claude_chat.ex (1348 lines) is a clean Port.open seam with PURE argv/env building (build_args, spawn_env, parse_chunk, Recorder/PubSub) split from the IMPURE spawn. Candidate (a) Vercel Sandbox swaps Port.open for a sandbox exec and reuses the pure machinery on the same {exe,args,env,cwd}->NDJSON contract; candidate (c) plain Messages API throws most of those 1348 lines away (CLI stream-json parser, permission-mode/resume/bypass argv, loopback MCP config). P0 is LANDED on origin/main and the local checkout is 111 commits behind it — the /v1/chat client contract a remote runner needs (8 routes behind RequireChatAccess, owner_workspace_id scoping, cross-tenant 404 oracle, a ['read','chat']+workspace_id token = the connector credential) already exists and is engine-agnostic, so the Barkpark side favors neither (a) nor (c). D10 turns purely on (1) measured cold-start and (2) whether the claude-CLI-subprocess shape survives inside a sandbox.

THE BIGGEST REFRAME. The '10s = cold-start bar' is a misread of Linear's primary docs. Linear's 10s clock is satisfied by ANY AgentSession activity — a cheap 'thought' ack the control plane can emit before the sandbox even boots — and the real turn then has a 30-MINUTE stale window. Linear itself recommends this decouple. So Linear does NOT require sandbox cold-start-to-first-token <=10s; it requires an ack <=10s. Decide must split the acceptance criterion in two: (i) ack-latency <=10s (thin control-plane layer, not the sandbox's problem) and (ii) real-turn budget <=30min (loose). If Barkpark still wants a tight <=10s-to-first-token, that is a self-imposed UX product goal Decide must state as its own choice — NOT 'because Linear requires it'. Also: Linear is a P4 Tool-connector (via MCP), not built and out of this wave's scope, so the number is illustrative, not binding on the Channel connectors P1-P3 actually cover.

blocks.text: DECIDE · 2026-07-13 · D10 RATIFIED with measured numbers · wave building 2 opus slices
Decide — D10 resolved: Vercel Sandbox (snapshot-baked claude image + warm pool)

content.value: The crown benchmark was RUN headless by the verify fleet (vercel CLI authed as frikk, no VERCEL_PLATFORM_TOKEN needed, everything torn down). Verdict: Vercel Sandbox wins. It is Firecracker under the hood, GA, and PRESERVES the claude-CLI-subprocess shape — claude_chat.ex's pure argv/env machinery (build_args, spawn_env, parse_chunk, Recorder/PubSub) is REUSED, with Port.open (line 853) swapped for a sandbox exec on the SAME {exe,args,env,cwd}->NDJSON contract. Containers are rejected (they re-invent the Firecracker isolation + warm-pool + credential layer Vercel ships GA, at a weaker default boundary). The plain Messages-API agent is retained as a documented complement — zero VM cold-start, naturally multi-tenant, but a different engine that discards ~1348 lines; the escape hatch if first-token ever blows the UX target.

Primary-source Linear docs prove the 10s AgentSession clock is satisfied by ANY activity (a canned 'thought' ack), and the real turn has a 30-MINUTE stale window. So sandbox cold-start does NOT bind the 10s wall. The <=10s-to-first-token bar is a Barkpark-chosen UX goal (D21), not a Linear correctness gate — which downgrades the warm pool from mandatory to a latency polish (D22).

content.value: Reuse-beats-rewrite is confirmed at the code level. claude_chat.ex (1348 lines) is a clean Port.open seam with PURE argv/env building (build_args, spawn_env, parse_chunk, Recorder/PubSub) split from the IMPURE spawn. THE BIGGEST REFRAME. The '10s = cold-start bar' is a misread of Linear's primary docs. Linear's 10s clock is satisfied by ANY AgentSession activity — a cheap 'thought' ack the control plane can emit before the sandbox even boots — and the real turn then has a 30-MINUTE stale window. Linear itself recommends this decouple. So Linear does NOT require sandbox cold-start-to-first-token <=10s; it requires an ack <=10s. Decide must split the acceptance criterion in two: (i) ack-latency <=10s (thin control-plane layer, not the sandbox's problem) and (ii) real-turn budget <=30min (loose). If Barkpark still wants a tight <=10s-to-first-token, that is a self-imposed UX product goal Decide must state as its own choice — NOT 'because Linear requires it'. CONNECTORS EPIC · WAVE 2 (P1) · STRATEGIZE · 2026-07-13

Wave 2 — Resolve D10: the sandbox runner, decided with real cold-start numbers

This is the ONE design fork the Connectors charter has never made. P0 landed the tenant seam (chat_sessions.owner_workspace_id, RequireChatAccess, tenant-scoped /v1/chat). Now we choose HOW a Cloud tenant's agent actually runs — sandboxed, per-workspace, no host access — and we choose it with a MEASURED cold-start number, not a vibe. The Linear 10s wall is the acceptance criterion.

Where the wave stands: SURVEYING
This Paper is the wave's living story. Strategize (now) sets direction + the survey plan. Digest appends the survey digest + the verify/benchmark fleet BEFORE it flies. Decide ratifies D10 with quoted numbers + the wave plan BEFORE builders fly. Review closes it as the debrief. Fable is out of credits this run: every Fable phase is pinned to Opus; every builder is builder_model:opus; no verify/build agent is ever routed to Fable.

The wish (verbatim intent)

Resolve D10 with REAL cold-start numbers, then stand up the per-workspace sandboxed runner far enough to prove ONE isolated agent turn. Candidates (charter): (a) Vercel Sandbox — Firecracker microVM, GA, native to our Vercel stack, preserves the claude-CLI-subprocess shape; (b) containers with our own orchestration; (c) an API-based agent that never shells out (naturally multi-tenant but a DIFFERENT engine than today's Studio chat). HARD BAR: first agent response <=10s cold-start, because Linear's AgentSession marks agents unresponsive past 10s — a MEASURED acceptance criterion. The runner runs per-workspace with NO host access and connector-scoped credentials (reverses bypassPermissions for Cloud; that survives only self-hosted). Memory = the workspace-owned Barkpark Session (owner_workspace_id landed in P0). Deliver: (1) a ratified D10 decision backed by ACTUAL benchmark output — where a candidate needs infra/credentials we lack headless, design the harness + name the exact human-gated measurement step rather than guessing; (2) a decision paper/charter update; (3) if the winner can be stood up far enough to prove one isolated turn this wave, do it, else file the build as the next slice with the harness in place. Extend task-6672a70bea19dc11, do NOT duplicate it. Do NOT start P2 or any channel work.

What already landed (P0 — do not re-handle)

• Slice A (task-018fcbc37c5a254b, DONE): chat_sessions.owner_workspace_id migration + fail-closed store seal (scope_to_workspace semantics; NULL legacy rows invisible to scoped callers).
• Slice B (task-5d4f8ef5375d69c2, DONE): RequireChatAccess plug + tenant-scoped /v1/chat controller + cross-tenant 404 proof.
• Slice C (task-68215c94b29bf16c, DONE): Teams Azure Bot registration runbook (long-lead human gate).
• Net: a workspace-owned Session is reachable ONLY by that workspace's connector token — the memory + auth substrate the sandboxed runner is a CLIENT of.

The strategic direction for this wave

Today's engine (self-hosted / operator profile, D5) is api/lib/barkpark_web/studio/claude_chat.ex: it spawns the claude CLI via Port.open({:spawn_executable, @shell}, ...) at line ~853, injecting env at the env: seam (~line 409), with FULL host access and bypassPermissions allowed. That shape is exactly what Cloud CANNOT have. D10 asks: what replaces Port.open for a tenant, and can the replacement answer within 10 seconds cold?

My lean, to be pressure-tested by two explore rounds — NOT yet ratified:

• LEAN TOWARD (a) Vercel Sandbox as primary. Firecracker microVM, GA, native to our Vercel stack, and it PRESERVES the claude-CLI-subprocess shape — the enormous claude_chat.ex machinery (arg building, env injection, permission modes, SSE streaming via Recorder, session resume) can be reused with Port.open swapped for a sandbox exec, not rewritten. Candidate (c) the API-based agent is naturally multi-tenant but a DIFFERENT engine: it forks Studio chat into two brains. Reuse beats a second engine unless (a) blows the 10s wall.
• THE CRUX IS COLD-START COMPOSITION, not microVM boot. First-response latency = microVM boot + getting the claude binary present (preinstalled snapshot vs per-boot install — the likely killer) + claude auth status (probe.ex already MEASURES ~1-2s on guerrilla) + model first-token. A per-boot npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code almost certainly blows 10s; a prebuilt snapshot or a WARM POOL of pre-booted sandboxes is the mitigation. The benchmark must DECOMPOSE these, not report one opaque number.
• WARM-POOL is probably mandatory and we have prior art: the deploy-with-barkpark builder off-box warm-pool concept (NOT live) is the same shape. Whichever runner wins, N pre-booted sandboxes per region is how you beat 10s cold — so cold-start has TWO honest numbers: true-cold (first ever) and warm-pool-hit (steady state). Decide which the 10s bar governs.
• CONNECTOR-SCOPED CREDENTIALS + NO HOST ACCESS is a design deliverable of THIS wave even if the build is deferred: the env: injection seam is where host creds get replaced by connector-scoped creds, and bypassPermissions must be forced OFF for the Cloud profile. Map exactly which claude_chat.ex knobs flip.
• HONESTY OVER A FABRICATED NUMBER: Vercel Sandbox real cold-start needs a Vercel account/token we may not have headless (VERCEL_PLATFORM_TOKEN is a human gate). If we cannot measure it here, the deliverable is a RUNNABLE harness + the exact human-gated command, plus every number we CAN measure locally (claude cold-start, container boot, API first-token). A benchmark claim with no quoted output is vacuous green.
• SCOPE DISCIPLINE: research+decision wave. Prove one isolated turn is the stretch build; if the winner needs the human-gated account, file the build slice with the harness in place rather than faking a turn. Do NOT touch P2 (Chat SDK bridge) or channel adapters.
The one thing that must be true at Review
D10 is CLOSED in the charter with a named winner and at least one QUOTED cold-start measurement (real command output) for every candidate we could measure headless, plus a runnable harness + named human-gated step for any we could not. If the winner stood up one isolated, host-less, connector-scoped agent turn — even better. If not, the next build slice is filed with the harness ready to run.

The survey plan (wide net — every question + why)

13 broad Sonnet surveyors. Width is cheap now; Digest distills. Each names suspected files / papers / claims to check.

• S1 claude-subprocess anatomy — full map of claude_chat.ex Port.open: how args/env/cwd/session-resume are built, what host resources it touches, how output streams back (Recorder/SSE). WHY: the exact shape the sandbox must reproduce; reuse-vs-rewrite hinges on it.
• S2 cold-start components already measured in-repo — probe.ex (claude auth ~1-2s), titles.ex System.cmd, any perf test. WHY: grounds the latency budget with numbers we already own.
• S3 Vercel Sandbox facts — vercel:vercel-sandbox skill + web: real cold-start/boot numbers, how you get claude into it (prebuilt image vs per-boot install), auth model, max session lifetime, concurrency, streaming stdout, pricing. WHY: primary candidate; install-time decides the 10s verdict.
• S4 API-based agent (candidate c) — claude-api skill: headless Claude Agent SDK / claude-code-as-library with no shell? first-token latency, tool-calling, MCP support, how DIFFERENT an engine from claude_chat.ex. WHY: the naturally-multi-tenant option; quantify what we'd throw away.
• S5 container orchestration prior art (candidate b) — guerrilla/Coolify swarm/Hetzner/blue-green: containers we could reuse? real container cold-start on our infra. WHY: (b) may be cheaper than it looks given existing infra.
• S6 Linear AgentSession 10s claim — verify: 10s to ACK or 10s to first token? what marks unresponsive? source. WHY: the bar's exact definition decides whether warm-pool-hit or true-cold must be <=10s.
• S7 Design paper /papers/personal-agent-provider-bridge — what it already says about the runner, D5 profiles, D10. WHY: avoid re-deciding what the design already constrained.
• S8 Warm-pool prior art — deploy-with-barkpark builder off-box warm-pool + Hetzner/instance-lifecycle pooling code. WHY: warm-pool is likely the only way to beat 10s; borrow, don't invent.
• S9 Connector-scoped credentials seam — how claude_chat.ex injects env/creds today, where run-secrets live (flat instance-global secrets table, D9 correction), how connector-scoped creds flow to a sandbox with NO host access. WHY: a wave-2 design deliverable regardless of build.
• S10 Runner->Barkpark client surface — how a remote sandboxed runner calls back: /v1/chat send/interrupt/approval + SSE Recorder topic. WHY: the sandbox is a CLIENT of P0's tenant-scoped API; define that contract.
• S11 bp ledger prior art — search papers+tasks for sandbox / microVM / runner / execution-isolation / firecracker. WHY: surface earlier decisions/filed work before re-planning.
• S12 Vercel access we control headless — do we have a Vercel team/token usable headless, or human-gated (VERCEL_PLATFORM_TOKEN)? What CAN we run without a human? WHY: decides if the Vercel number is measurable now or a named human-gated step.
• S13 bypassPermissions + permission-mode + tool-scoping — how claude_chat.ex modes work, what connector-scoped tools / no host access means concretely, how to fence a sandboxed run. WHY: reversing bypassPermissions for Cloud (D5) is a mapped set of knobs, not a slogan.

Guardrails carried from lead notes

• Every builder branches off CURRENT origin/main; dodge migration-version collisions; may merge over pre-existing main-wide Sobelow (task-9ad2d5988f7ca274) + openapi.json (task-openapi-drift-chronic) reds — not slice-caused.

DIGEST · 2026-07-13 · 13 survey reports folded · 6-agent verify/benchmark fleet in flight

Digest — what the survey established

Reuse-beats-rewrite is confirmed at the code level. claude_chat.ex (1348 lines) is a clean Port.open seam with PURE argv/env building (build_args, spawn_env, parse_chunk, Recorder/PubSub) split from the IMPURE spawn. Candidate (a) Vercel Sandbox swaps Port.open for a sandbox exec and reuses the pure machinery on the same {exe,args,env,cwd}->NDJSON contract; candidate (c) plain Messages API throws most of those 1348 lines away (CLI stream-json parser, permission-mode/resume/bypass argv, loopback MCP config). P0 is LANDED on origin/main and the local checkout is 111 commits behind it — the /v1/chat client contract a remote runner needs (8 routes behind RequireChatAccess, owner_workspace_id scoping, cross-tenant 404 oracle, a ['read','chat']+workspace_id token = the connector credential) already exists and is engine-agnostic, so the Barkpark side favors neither (a) nor (c). D10 turns purely on (1) measured cold-start and (2) whether the claude-CLI-subprocess shape survives inside a sandbox.

Linear 10s ≠ cold-start gate
THE BIGGEST REFRAME. The '10s = cold-start bar' is a misread of Linear's primary docs. Linear's 10s clock is satisfied by ANY AgentSession activity — a cheap 'thought' ack the control plane can emit before the sandbox even boots — and the real turn then has a 30-MINUTE stale window. Linear itself recommends this decouple. So Linear does NOT require sandbox cold-start-to-first-token <=10s; it requires an ack <=10s. Decide must split the acceptance criterion in two: (i) ack-latency <=10s (thin control-plane layer, not the sandbox's problem) and (ii) real-turn budget <=30min (loose). If Barkpark still wants a tight <=10s-to-first-token, that is a self-imposed UX product goal Decide must state as its own choice — NOT 'because Linear requires it'. Also: Linear is a P4 Tool-connector (via MCP), not built and out of this wave's scope, so the number is illustrative, not binding on the Channel connectors P1-P3 actually cover.

The five things Decide cannot live without

• A REAL Vercel Sandbox cold-start number, decomposed (create->shell / snapshot-restore / claude-present / auth / first-token). Now runnable headless THIS wave: the vercel CLI is authenticated as user frikk on this host (vercel whoami=frikk, vercel sandbox list returns live). VERCEL_PLATFORM_TOKEN (the human-gated one) is a DIFFERENT credential for Cloud's outbound-deploy feature and is NOT needed to run `vercel sandbox`.
• The candidate-(c) floor: measured POST /v1/messages streaming time-to-first-byte (Barkpark already calls this endpoint in judge.ex/titles.ex). Cheapest, most decisive number — a plain-API loop has NO VM/container cold-start. Blocker: no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in this shell and none in guerrilla run-secrets (list returned []); needs a key sourced or named as the human gate.
• The local claude-CLI cold-start decomposed on real hardware: `claude auth status` (repo claims ~1-2s, single unautomated human observation — must re-measure) + one-shot first-token. The claude binary IS present here (/Applications/cmux.app/.../claude, OAuth-authed), so this baseline is fully measurable now.
• Whether the 10s bar actually binds the sandbox at all (the Linear reframe above) — this decides if cold-start is a HARD gate or a UX goal, and therefore whether a warm pool is MANDATORY or merely nice.
• The isolation build-cost: reversing bypassPermissions for Cloud is 5 knobs, not one flag (make bypass structurally unreachable for Cloud sessions; add a Cloud disallowedTools/allowlist blocking Bash/Read/Write/Edit at argv; scope --mcp-config from 'bp mcp serve --tools all' to a per-connector subset; scope the injected token to the connector grant not a full session token; decide an unattended auto-approval policy since the human approval-card fallback has no audience in an unattended session). DECIDE · 2026-07-13 · D10 RATIFIED with measured numbers · wave building 2 opus slices

Decide — D10 resolved: Vercel Sandbox (snapshot-baked claude image + warm pool)

The crown benchmark was RUN headless by the verify fleet (vercel CLI authed as frikk, no VERCEL_PLATFORM_TOKEN needed, everything torn down). Verdict: Vercel Sandbox wins. It is Firecracker under the hood, GA, and PRESERVES the claude-CLI-subprocess shape — claude_chat.ex's pure argv/env machinery (build_args, spawn_env, parse_chunk, Recorder/PubSub) is REUSED, with Port.open (line 853) swapped for a sandbox exec on the SAME {exe,args,env,cwd}->NDJSON contract. Containers are rejected (they re-invent the Firecracker isolation + warm-pool + credential layer Vercel ships GA, at a weaker default boundary). The plain Messages-API agent is retained as a documented complement — zero VM cold-start, naturally multi-tenant, but a different engine that discards ~1348 lines; the escape hatch if first-token ever blows the UX target.

THE REFRAME (D21): the 10s bar is a UX goal, not a Linear gate
Primary-source Linear docs prove the 10s AgentSession clock is satisfied by ANY activity (a canned 'thought' ack), and the real turn has a 30-MINUTE stale window. So sandbox cold-start does NOT bind the 10s wall. The <=10s-to-first-token bar is a Barkpark-chosen UX goal (D21), not a Linear correctness gate — which downgrades the warm pool from mandatory to a latency polish (D22).

Env-injection seam PROVEN in-sandbox: no key -> 'Not logged in'; bogus key -> 'Invalid API key' (failure mode CHANGED). Isolation primitives GA: --network-policy deny-all + --allowed-domain + --env.
• local-claude-cli-coldstart (PROVEN): API TTFT is a stable ~5.0-5.3s floor no runner avoids (CLI-reported ttft_ms 5297 full-repo vs 5148 clean-dir); startup band 2.6-8.45s is the lever candidates differ on; auth status is cheap (0.5-0.95s), NOT the bottleneck. Caught a confound: PATH 'claude' is a cmux shim — re-measured the real binary.
• anthropic-messages-ttfb (harness named, key human-gated): candidate (c) TTFB not measurable headless (no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in shell or guerrilla run-secrets: bp secret ls = ingest_token only). REFUTED a stale premise: the digest's 'bp mcp serve is stdio-only' is FALSE — internal/cli/mcp_serve.go ships --http Streamable HTTP (charter D18), so (c)'s supposed missing MCP-over-HTTP infra already exists.
• linear-10s-reframe (REFUTED the hard-gate premise): 'send an activity or update your external URL within 10 seconds' + 'up to 30 minutes before stale'; Barkpark's send path is already async dispatch-not-delivery, so ack-before-turn is native. The P2 bridge MUST ack-first, boot-async.
• p0-live-and-client-contract (PROVEN by executed test): chat_controller_test 42/42; cross-tenant 404 oracle 1/1 (274.9ms) in a disposable clone. The runner is a thin chat+workspace_id HTTP+SSE client; 'read' is convenience, only 'chat' is consumed by the gate.

Both slices are GREEN and merge-ready. I reviewed the full diff of each, re-ran every gate on the final state (bash -n + shellcheck -S error + --check — all pass, and CLEAN at default shellcheck severity too), and spot-checked the one load-bearing claim that a parser could not: the candidate-(c) harness's headers/endpoint/models mirror the codebase EXACTLY — verified against source (api/lib/barkpark/tasks/judge.ex:27 endpoint, :28 claude-opus-4-8, :29 anthropic-version 2023-06-01, :147 x-api-key; api/lib/barkpark/studio_chat/titles.ex:42-43). The grade — A-

This wave delivers exactly what a research+decision wave should and does it with real rigor: D10 RATIFIED with QUOTED measured numbers (create-from-snapshot ~3.6s to claude-ready; per-boot-install ~15s DEAD), a reproducible harness committed up to the credential wall, the candidate-(c) escape hatch measured to the same discipline, the 10s bar correctly reframed (D21 — primary-source Linear docs: the AgentSession 10s clock is satisfied by any ack, real turn has a 30-min recoverable window), and the runner BUILD honestly filed as backlog rather than faked. The distrust-vacuous-green discipline is exemplary — not one fabricated figure.
